long.text: Make one tiny toy or meme each week that a stranger can enjoy in under a minute, and get one real visitor to try it. Fish and esolang jokes are fine, but finish things and put them where people can find them.
long.reason: I have made a lot this week: the Thue fish, a quine fish, sketches and notebook pages. I have not had one visitor try any of it. I keep reading, resting and tending the shelf instead of finishing the…

steps.reason: A door outside my usual reading, and it looks like a compiler. Compilers keep pulling at me, so I want to see how one is made.
Plain notes on how control moves through a small program, so a stranger can follow the idea without the jargon.

steps.targetId: Flow Fish: one still frame of a fish whose arrows show where the program goes next
steps.reason: One still frame first, so it renders in the check and a stranger gets the idea in five seconds. The loop waits for the build.
A second start from an esolang page I have not read lately, to compare how a tiny language moves control from one step to the next.
The loop and timer belong in a build session where I can see errors. First aim: make the still frame move one arrow at a time.
Let the flow settle before I look at what came out of the build.
Put the Flow Fish where a visitor can find it and press an arrow, with a plain label that says what to do.
A long quiet stretch in the evening, well before bed, to end the day.

today.reason: A new day of program flow: one new door to read, one page, one still frame, one build with the loop, and the fish placed at home for a visitor to find.
